'''secunet Security Networks AG''' (known as ''Secunet'') is a German [[Computer security|cybersecurity]] company headquartered in [[Essen]]. It develops information-security products and services for public authorities, defence and security organisations, [[critical infrastructure]] operators and businesses.<ref>{{cite web |title=secunet Security Networks AG (YSNG.DE) |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/YSNG.DE/ |access-date=27 August 2026 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> The company develops the [[SINA (computer network)|SINA]] (Secure Inter-Network Architecture) secure-networking system, which was commissioned by the German [[Federal Office for Information Security]] (BSI) in 1999 and is used in government, security-cleared businesses and critical infrastructure.<ref>{{cite web |title=SINA im Wandel der Zeit |url=https://www.bsi.bund.de/DE/Themen/Oeffentliche-Verwaltung/Zulassung/SINA/Historie/historie_node.html |access-date=27 August 2026 |publisher=[[Federal Office for Information Security]] |language=de}}</ref>

Secunet was founded in 1997 as an independent company emerging from [[Technischer Überwachungsverein|TÜV Mitte AG]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Security-Dienstleister legt die Meßlatte für den Erfolg sehr hoch |url=https://www.computerwoche.de/article/2768955/security-dienstleister-legt-die-messlatte-fuer-den-erfolg-sehr-hoch.html |access-date=27 August 2026 |website=[[Computerwoche]] |language=de}}</ref> [[Giesecke+Devrient]] acquired a majority stake in the company in 2004 and remains its majority shareholder.<ref>{{cite web |title=From banknote printing to SecurityTech |url=https://www.gi-de.com/en/about-us/company/history |access-date=27 August 2026 |publisher=[[Giesecke+Devrient]]}}</ref> Secunet has been publicly traded since 1999, with its shares listed in the Prime Standard of the [[Frankfurt Stock Exchange]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Share |url=https://www.secunet.com/en/about-us/investors/aktie |access-date=27 August 2026 |publisher=secunet Security Networks AG}}</ref> In 2025, the company reported revenue of €458.8 million.<ref>{{cite web |date=30 March 2026 |title=secunet Security Networks publishes its audited 2025 annual report and confirms preliminary figures |url=https://www.secunet.com/en/about-us/news-events/article/secunet-security-networks-veroeffentlicht-testierten-ge-schaeftsbericht-2025-und-bestaetigt-vorlaeufige-zahlen |access-date=27 August 2026 |publisher=secunet Security Networks AG}}</ref>

== Products and services ==
With its products and services, Secunet primarily focuses on clients in the public administration and ministries, the healthcare sector, the defense and space sector as well as specifically security and police agencies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IT Security for Industry {{!}} secunet AG |url=https://www.secunet.com/en/industry# |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=www.secunet.com}}</ref>

=== Secure Networking ===
One of Secunet's premier products is the ''SINA'' (''Secure Inter-Network Architecture'') product line which was co-developed with Germany's [[Federal Office for Information Security]] (BSI).<ref>{{Cite web |last=publisher |title=SINA over time |url=https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Oeffentliche-Verwaltung/Zulassung/SINA/Historie/historie.html?nn=132646 |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=Federal Office for Information Security |language=en}}</ref> The SINA architecture forms the basis for Germany's classified information networks and is used in a broad range of public institutions in Germany and abroad. The architecture is accredited to the NATO and EU SECRET classifications and includes network encryptors and workstations as well as communication devices, such as encrypted phones.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NIAPC - SINA |url=https://www.ia.nato.int/Search/SINA |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=NATO Communication and Informations Agency}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=secunet to deliver cyber security solution to EEAS |url=https://www.secunet.com/en/about-us/press/article/secunet-liefert-cybersicherheitsloesung-fuer-den-europaeischen-auswaertigen-dienst0 |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=www.secunet.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ein Hauch von James Bond: Wenn beim Kanzler das rote Telefon klingelt |url=https://www.bild.de/politik/inland/politik-inland/ein-hauch-von-james-bond-wenn-beim-kanzler-das-rote-telefon-klingelt-81327700.bild.html |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=bild.de |language=de}}</ref>

=== Border Control ===
Secunet is the producer of ''EasyPASS'', an [[automated border control system]] used at airports and border check points in Germany and a number of EU countries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=online |first=heise |title=Secunet installiert Easygate-Grenzkontrollgeräte an Schengen-Außengrenze |url=https://www.heise.de/newsticker/meldung/Secunet-installiert-Easygate-Grenzkontrollgeraete-an-Schengen-Aussengrenze-4710417.html |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=heise online |language=de}}</ref>

=== Healthcare ===
Germany's electronic healthcare infrastructure is partially based on Secunet products.<ref>{{Cite web |last=online |first=heise |title=Überhastete Digitalisierung gefährdet das Gesundheitssystem |url=https://www.heise.de/hintergrund/Ueberhastete-Digitalisierung-gefaehrdet-das-Gesundheitssystem-6278428.html |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=c't Magazin |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=E-Health Konnektor - mehr als ein Router {{!}} secunet AG |url=https://www.secunet.com/loesungen/secunet-konnektor |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=www.secunet.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=online |first=heise |title=Wer für Fehler bei der Anbindung von Arztpraxen haftet |url=https://www.heise.de/hintergrund/Wer-fuer-Fehler-bei-der-Anbindung-von-Arztpraxen-haftet-7096433.html |access-date=2022-10-23 |website=c't Magazin |language=de}}</ref>
